Contrast Ratio Checker

A calculator for the contrast ratio between two colours, with the WCAG pass or fail for text.

Jump to the explanation

A calculator that measures the contrast ratio between a text colour and a background colour, the number the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines use to judge readable text. It is for designers and developers checking a palette. Type or pick two colours; the ratio and the pass or fail verdicts update at once. Everything runs in your browser.

7.00:1 contrast

    Sample text in the two colours: the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.

    How it works

    What the ratio measures

    The contrast ratio compares how much light two colours send to your eye. It runs from 1:1, a colour against itself, to 21:1, black against white. The Web Content Accessibility Guidelines, WCAG for short, use it as the test for readable text, because people with low vision or a dim screen lose the difference between two colours long before you do.

    How it is computed

    Each colour first becomes a relative luminance: a number from 0 for black to 1 for white. The red, green and blue channels are turned from screen values back into light (the sRGB curve), then weighted by how bright each looks to the eye: green counts for about 72 percent, red for 21 and blue for 7. That is why pure blue text feels dark and pure green feels bright.

    The ratio is then the lighter luminance plus 0.05, divided by the darker luminance plus 0.05. The 0.05 stands for a little glare on any real screen, and it is the reason the scale stops at 21 instead of going on forever.

    What passes

    • Normal text needs 4.5:1 for level AA and 7:1 for level AAA.
    • Large text (about 24 pixels, or 19 pixels in bold) needs 3:1 for AA and 4.5:1 for AAA.
    • Icons and the borders of inputs need 3:1.

    The ratio is shown with two decimals and is never rounded up: grey #777777 on white is 4.478:1, so it shows as 4.47 and fails AA, even though it looks close enough.

    Limits

    This tool checks solid sRGB colours given as hex codes. It cannot judge text on a photo or a gradient, transparent colours, thin fonts or colour blindness, and it uses the WCAG 2 formula, not newer proposals such as APCA. Treat a pass as a minimum, not a guarantee that everyone can read your text. Nothing you type leaves this page.

    About & making of

    The formulas come straight from the WCAG 2.2 definitions; twelve known-answer tests from WCAG and WebAIM run in the page and in QA (window.__sedSelfTest).

    Sources

    • Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2: the definitions of relative luminance and contrast ratio, and the 4.5:1, 3:1 and 7:1 thresholds
    • Understanding Success Criterion 1.4.3: Contrast (Minimum): what counts as large text, and that a ratio is never rounded up
    • WebAIM: Contrast Checker: reference values for the known-answer tests, such as 4.48:1 for #777777 on white
